headline_marked: [[Cape Verde captain under investigation]] for alleged rape ahead of Argentina match
headline: Cape Verde captain under investigation for alleged rape ahead of Argentina match
summary: Ryan Mendes, 36, faces a potential 20-year prison sentence if convicted of the March incident involving a Brazilian interpreter in New Zealand. FIFA is monitoring the situation.
details: Cape Verde captain Ryan Mendes is under investigation for alleged rape, casting a shadow over the team's historic match against Argentina. The 36-year-old faces up to 20 years in prison under New Zealand law if convicted.
The accusation stems from an incident in March during a tri-nation tournament in New Zealand. A Brazilian woman, hired as an interpreter for the Cape Verde team, filed the complaint.

The woman alleges she was invited to a room at the team's hotel for what she believed was a professional meeting, but found it to be a party. She claims Mendes forcibly entered her room and raped her after she returned to her own room feeling unwell.

A formal complaint was filed in an Auckland court on April 10. The New Zealand Football Federation officially informed FIFA last month, with the global governing body reportedly monitoring the situation closely.

The victim initially sought help from the Cape Verde Football Federation but received no response before approaching local police. Neither Mendes, his lawyer, nor the Cape Verde Football Federation has issued an official statement regarding the allegations, according to 'O Globo'.

headline_marked: [[Witnesses recount Turag chase as police deny]] activists jumped into river; three bodies recovered
headline: Witnesses recount Turag chase as police deny activists jumped into river; three bodies recovered
summary: Rumours of activists fleeing police into the Turag River on June 22 intensified after three decomposed bodies were recovered, though authorities deny any connection to the alleged incident.
details: Rumours have spread for nearly a week about activists of the banned Bangladesh Chhatra League disappearing after allegedly jumping into the Turag River to escape a sudden police raid in Ashulia on June 22. Police firmly dismiss these claims as "baseless," stating they only arrested seven people from a procession and no such incident occurred.

However, witnesses present beside the river paint a more complicated picture. While none could confirm drownings, several told bdnews24.com they saw people leap into the Turag after police chased a trawler attempting to dock near the Ashulia cattle market.

The accounts gained renewed attention after three highly decomposed bodies were recovered from the Turag over the following days. Police maintain none of these deaths were connected to the procession or the alleged chase.

One of the recovered individuals was 18-year-old Mohammad Sumon. His family searched for him after he disappeared on June 22 but was not informed by police of any alleged fall into the river, identifying his body only after its recovery days later.

Inspector Mohammad Asgar Hossain of Ashulia Police stated they are repeating information from an unnatural death case filed by a complainant and has "no knowledge" of witness claims about police chasing people into the river.

Dhaka SP Shamima Parveen and the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) have also rejected claims of suspicious deaths or political connections to the recovered bodies, warning of legal action against those spreading false information.
Legal experts are now demanding an independent judicial inquiry to uncover the truth behind the missing boatmen and the conflicting accounts surrounding the events of June 22.
